paragraphs.text: Borrowing: Anyone who lives, works or studies in the district can join Ashgrove Community Library free of charge. Bring one form of photo identification and something showing your current address, such as a recent utility bill, to the front desk, and your card will be printed while you wait. Adult members may borrow up to twelve items at a time, including books, audiobooks and DVDs. Most items are lent for three weeks, but new releases and DVDs must be returned after seven days because demand for them is high. You can renew an item twice, online or by phone, provided nobody else has reserved it. We no longer charge fines on children's books, although adults who return items late pay a small daily charge. Returns can be made at any time using the book drop beside the main entrance, even when the building is closed.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: E-books and digital services: Your library card also gives you access to our digital collection, which includes thousands of e-books, e-audiobooks and current magazines. First, download the free LibraryLink app on your phone or tablet and sign in with your card number and four-digit PIN. If you have forgotten your PIN, staff at the front desk can reset it, but for security reasons this cannot be done over the phone. Up to six digital titles can be borrowed at once, and they disappear from your device automatically when the loan period ends, so there is never anything to bring back. Popular titles often have a waiting list; you will receive an email as soon as your turn comes, and you then have two days to accept the loan before it passes to the next person. Anyone who feels unsure about using the app can book a free half-hour session with one of our volunteer 'digital helpers', who are available on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Study rooms: On the first floor there are four quiet study rooms, each seating up to six people, as well as a single silent room with individual desks. The group rooms are ideal for revision sessions, small meetings or job interviews held by video call, and each is equipped with a large wall screen and a whiteboard. Members may book a room for a maximum of three hours per day, either online or at the front desk, up to a fortnight in advance. Bookings are free for members; non-members may use a room for a fee of £5 an hour. Please arrive on time: if nobody has checked in within fifteen minutes of the start of a booking, the room may be given to someone else. Food is not permitted in any study area, though drinks in bottles with a lid are welcome. The silent room cannot be reserved and is available on a first-come, first-served basis.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Children's events: Our children's area is busy all week. Rhyme Time, for babies and toddlers with their parents or carers, runs every Monday and Wednesday at 10.30 a.m. and lasts about half an hour; no booking is needed. Older children aged five to eleven can join the Saturday Story Club, where they listen to stories, play word games and make simple crafts. Because places are limited to twenty, families should reserve a spot in advance. During the summer holidays, children are invited to take part in our reading challenge: participants who finish six books receive a certificate and a medal at a celebration event in September. Tevita Faleolo, who coordinates our children's events, believes the challenge helps young readers keep up their skills during the long break from school, and he hopes more families will join this year. Please note that children under eight must be supervised by an adult at all times while in the library.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Opening hours and other information: The library is open from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturdays; it is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout the building, and printing and photocopying cost 10p per black-and-white page. Branch manager Ottavia Kerimova encourages members to share their ideas: a suggestion box is located next to the lift, and comments can also be left on our website. 'Many of our recent improvements, including longer Saturday hours, came directly from users,' she explains.
paragraphs.label: E

section.text:
Welcome to Ashgrove Community Library

A. Borrowing: Anyone who lives, works or studies in the district can join Ashgrove Community Library free of charge. Bring one form of photo identification and something showing your current address, such as a recent utility bill, to the front desk, and your card will be printed while you wait. Adult members may borrow up to twelve items at a time, including books, audiobooks and DVDs. Most items are lent for three weeks, but new releases and DVDs must be returned after seven days because demand for them is high. You can renew an item twice, online or by phone, provided nobody else has reserved it. We no longer charge fines on children's books, although adults who return items late pay a small daily charge. Returns can be made at any time using the book drop beside the main entrance, even when the building is closed.

B. E-books and digital services: Your library card also gives you access to our digital collection, which includes thousands of e-books, e-audiobooks and current magazines. First, download the free LibraryLink app on your phone or tablet and sign in with your card number and four-digit PIN. If you have forgotten your PIN, staff at the front desk can reset it, but for security reasons this cannot be done over the phone. Up to six digital titles can be borrowed at once, and they disappear from your device automatically when the loan period ends, so there is never anything to bring back. Popular titles often have a waiting list; you will receive an email as soon as your turn comes, and you then have two days to accept the loan before it passes to the next person. Anyone who feels unsure about using the app can book a free half-hour session with one of our volunteer 'digital helpers', who are available on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

C. Study rooms: On the first floor there are four quiet study rooms, each seating up to six people, as well as a single silent room with individual desks. The group rooms are ideal for revision sessions, small meetings or job interviews held by video call, and each is equipped with a large wall screen and a whiteboard. Members may book a room for a maximum of three hours per day, either online or at the front desk, up to a fortnight in advance. Bookings are free for members; non-members may use a room for a fee of £5 an hour. Please arrive on time: if nobody has checked in within fifteen minutes of the start of a booking, the room may be given to someone else. Food is not permitted in any study area, though drinks in bottles with a lid are welcome. The silent room cannot be reserved and is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

D. Children's events: Our children's area is busy all week. Rhyme Time, for babies and toddlers with their parents or carers, runs every Monday and Wednesday at 10.30 a.m. and lasts about half an hour; no booking is needed. Older children aged five to eleven can join the Saturday Story Club, where they listen to stories, play word games and make simple crafts. Because places are limited to twenty, families should reserve a spot in advance. During the summer holidays, children are invited to take part in our reading challenge: participants who finish six books receive a certificate and a medal at a celebration event in September. Tevita Faleolo, who coordinates our children's events, believes the challenge helps young readers keep up their skills during the long break from school, and he hopes more families will join this year. Please note that children under eight must be supervised by an adult at all times while in the library.

E. Opening hours and other information: The library is open from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturdays; it is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout the building, and printing and photocopying cost 10p per black-and-white page. Branch manager Ottavia Kerimova encourages members to share their ideas: a suggestion box is located next to the lift, and comments can also be left on our website.
